moduleTitle: Automating Mobile Apps on TMA — Part 1: AVD Setup & TMA Integration
learningObjectives: List the steps required to configure an Android Virtual Device (AVD) using Android Studio and integrate it with Tricentis Mobile Agent (TMA) for automation testing.
Create an Android Virtual Device (AVD) in Android Studio from scratch, choosing a device definition and system image deliberately rather than by default.
Boot the AVD and confirm it's genuinely ready for automation, not just visually running.
Integrate the AVD with the Tricentis Mobile Agent and confirm it appears Ready in the TMA console.
Wire the AVD's identifier into Tosca's DeviceName TCP correctly.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: From virtual-device creation to automation validation

elements.term: From 'an emulator exists' to 'TMA can drive it'
elements.description: A virtual device has separate configuration, boot, discovery and automation checks. Seeing its screen does not prove that the Agent can create a session or launch the test application.

elements.text: This is an independent local setup guide based on accessible product documentation. The original Academy recording and its exact exercise sequence were not available for comparison.

bulletPoints: An AVD that boots to the home screen is a necessary but not sufficient condition — TMA integration is a separate, deliberate step.

elements.title: AVD Manager walkthrough
items: Open Android Studio’s Device Manager using the menu available in the installed version.
Click Create Virtual Device, then pick a device definition — a specific phone profile (screen size, density, hardware buttons) such as Pixel 7 or Pixel 8.
Select a supported API level and compatible system-image architecture, downloading the image if needed.
Review the AVD configuration and use an identifiable profile name. Keep the profile name distinct from its runtime adb serial.
Finish the wizard, then launch the AVD from the Device Manager and wait for a full boot to the home screen — not just the boot animation completing.

elements.term: Picking the system image on purpose
elements.description: Choose an image that supports the application’s minimum SDK and required libraries, the intended coverage target and the Agent’s supported OS range. An emulator image is not evidence of identical physical-device behavior.

elements.text: Google documents matching image/host architecture for VM acceleration: x86/x86_64 on x86_64 hosts and arm64-v8a on ARM64 hosts. Do not assume an incompatible image will launch successfully through translation or infer rendering glitches from architecture alone.

bulletPoints: Device definition = hardware profile. System image = Android version + ABI. Both are deliberate choices, not defaults to click through.
Check supported host/image combinations and VM acceleration rather than promising fallback translation.

elements.title: From booted AVD to TMA-ready device
items: Run the Android emulator and Agent on the same supported host for the documented TMA setup.
Open the configured Agent web interface and inspect Device management; do not assume the Appium port is also every REST/UI endpoint.
Confirm the AVD appears in the device list with status Ready — not Offline, not absent entirely.
Inspect the runtime adb serial and the target value required by the selected Tosca connection. For adb, emulator-5554 corresponds to console port 5554, while its paired adb port is normally 5555.

elements.text: If the Agent does not detect the emulator, inspect adb detection, supported versions and Agent logs. A required universal AVD-before-Agent startup order is not established by these guides.

elements.description: Tosca’s device table specifies the displayed full emulator name for an Android emulator; other connection cases use reported device IDs. Use the value required by the actual connection and verify it with a minimal test. Do not interchange the AVD profile name and adb serial blindly.

bulletPoints: Distinguish AVD profile name, displayed target name and runtime adb serial.
Verify boot, Agent detection and session/application opening separately.
Console and adb ports are distinct; re-check the runtime target after relaunch.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming a booted emulator is automatically TMA-ready
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Seeing the AVD's home screen rendered in Android Studio and moving straight to Tosca without checking the TMA console.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check Agent detection and then a minimal session/application launch. A visible or Ready device does not isolate every possible failure.

examPitfalls.title: Mismatching system image ABI to host CPU
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Picking an x86_64 system image on an Apple Silicon Mac (or arm64-v8a on an Intel/AMD machine) and blaming Tosca or TMA for a sluggish, unstable emulator.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the documented compatible host/image architecture for VM acceleration. An architecture mismatch does not prove a particular slow-translation or rendering symptom.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming the emulator-#### identifier is permanent
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Hardcoding a DeviceName TCP to emulator-5554 and being surprised when, after relaunching the AVD, TMA reports a different or missing device.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the runtime serial and the connection-specific Tosca target value after relaunch. Console and adb ports differ; a profile name is not an adb serial.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An AVD is visibly running and shows its home screen in Android Studio, but Tosca fails to connect to it. What should be checked first?

options.text: Whether the AVD appears as Ready in the TMA console's device list.
Whether the AVD has enough storage space.
Whether Tosca Commander needs to be reinstalled.
Whether the host machine needs a reboot.

practiceQuiz.hint: A visually booted emulator and a TMA-visible device are two separate checks.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Checking Agent detection is a useful first investigation among these choices. It does not itself prove session health or isolate all configuration, driver and app failures.

optionExplanations.A: Agent detection should be verified separately from visual boot.
optionExplanations.B: The symptom does not establish storage as the first cause.
optionExplanations.C: Reinstallation is not justified before examining the connection.
optionExplanations.D: A full host reboot is not yet justified by the evidence.

practiceQuiz.scenario: For the adb serial emulator-5554, which port does 5554 identify in the documented console/adb pair?

options.text: A name manually chosen when creating the AVD.
The emulator console port; the paired adb port is normally 5555.
The Android API level of the system image.

practiceQuiz.hint: Console and adb use different ports.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented default pair uses console 5554 and adb 5555. The runtime serial is not the AVD profile name, API level or screen resolution.

optionExplanations.A: The profile name is separate from the runtime serial.
optionExplanations.B: This identifies the console side of the documented port pair.
optionExplanations.C: API level does not define this runtime port number.
optionExplanations.D: Resolution does not define this port number.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which image architecture matches an ARM64 host in Google’s documented VM-acceleration requirements?

options.text: Any architecture, because translation always works
arm64-v8a, with the other acceleration prerequisites met
The screen-resolution value determines the CPU architecture
Tosca Remote mode changes the host CPU architecture

practiceQuiz.rationale: The ARM64 row specifies arm64-v8a images. Other host and hypervisor requirements still apply; mismatched images are not guaranteed to run through translation.

optionExplanations.A: Universal translation support is not documented.
optionExplanations.B: This matches the ARM64 system-image requirement.
optionExplanations.C: Screen dimensions do not select the CPU architecture.
optionExplanations.D: Connection topology does not change CPU architecture.

quickRecap.value: Choose a hardware profile and compatible image, then review and launch the AVD.
Use supported host/image combinations and verify VM acceleration prerequisites.
Verify boot, Agent discovery and minimal session/app opening as separate checks.
adb serial emulator-5554 corresponds to console 5554; paired adb is normally 5555.
Use the connection-specific Tosca target value; profile names and adb serials are distinct.
